contact.name: Steven Reed
contact.designation: President of the American Optometric Association
contact.evidence_quote: “Getting an eye exam once a year is likely to result in earlier diagnosis of eye and vision problems, the prevention or reduction in vision loss, as well as improved health-related quality of life,” says Steven Reed, O.D., president of the American Optometric Association (AOA).

alternates.evidence_quote: By the time you hit your 40s, it’s not uncommon to be diagnosed with presbyopia, or “trouble seeing objects up close,” says Karen Squier, O.D. She’s the chief of low vision services at the Eye Center at Southern College of Optometry in Memphis, Tennessee. alternates.evidence_quote: Whether you choose glasses, contacts or both depends on your prescription and lifestyle, says Viola Kanevsky, O.D.
